A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIMOS and contain 17 readable pages, including supplementary Sections A–F and references. Text, equations, tables, and figures support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original DIMOS benchmark results in Table 2, component and backbone ablations in Tables 3–4, and supplementary analyses in Figure 5 and Tables 7–9.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, qualitative comparisons, and main-text and supplementary ablations reported in v1.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses, training procedure, and inference method are unchanged. Figure 2 corrects the depiction of translation and cross-type attention already specified in v1, without establishing a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate moving instance segmentation on MouseSIS, SEVD-Fixed, and EVIMO with the same domains and scenarios. Supplementary dataset coverage is identical.

E2.justification: IDOL, ModelMixSort, and EvInsMOS remain the comparators for each dataset in Table 2 and in the qualitative comparisons. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: Training budgets, batch size, input resolutions, preprocessing, metrics, and ablation configurations are identical in Section 4 and the supplementary material.

E4.justification: The component and backbone ablations, feature-similarity analysis, module-depth studies, and qualitative examples are unchanged, including Figure 5 and supplementary Tables 7–9.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical and qualitative results are retained. For example, Table 2 reports the same DIMOS mIoUins values of 70.25%, 62.05%, and 72.08% on MouseSIS, SEVD-Fixed, and EVIMO, respectively; supplementary results also match.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and loss formulations, including Equation (7) and supplementary Section C, are unchanged. Correcting translator labels in Figure 2 does not alter the underlying mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims about dual disentanglement, cross-modal alignment, and improved small-instance segmentation.

C2.justification: The interpretations of experimental gains and module-depth effects are unchanged. Section 5 retains the same limitation concerning dependence on synchronized, paired modalities.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 and supplementary Sections A and D retain the same architecture specifications, hyperparameters, hardware, and preprocessing details. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, reference list, and positioning relative to prior segmentation and multimodal methods are identical.

P1.justification: The marginal arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 11 June 2026 to v2 dated 11 August 2026. Body prose, headings, and main-text and supplementary organization remain identical.

P2.justification: Figure 2 swaps the Ta1/Ta2 and Tm1/Tm2 labels to match Equation (7), adds cross-branch arrows depicting appearance–motion attention, and makes small graphical adjustments. Other figures and tables are unchanged.

improvement.justification: Figure 2 now matches Equation (7)'s translator directions and explicitly depicts the previously described cross-type attention connections. These corrections modestly improve technical clarity and internal consistency; the method, experimental evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged.
